subject: Latency SLO: temporal boundaries & fallback commitments

Subject: Latency SLO: temporal boundaries & fallback commitments

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinX is excited about Redwood's hosted API and the latency profiles you showed. As we prepare procurement and legal, we need to nail down the p50/p95 commitments and how those are measured. Two specific asks from engineering and procurement: 

1) Measurement horizon: we want a short rolling window for operational guarantees (5 minute rolling for p50/p95) during peak sale events, but understand Redwood currently uses longer aggregation windows. Can you outline options and the downside/risk to short measurement windows?

2) Exception handling & fallbacks: during planned regional campaigns (e.g., Black Friday-like spikes) we need a clear carveout/rollback playbook and a fallback to a lower-cost model variant with defined latency bounds. What are typical carveout durations you can safely commit to, and how will failovers be signalled?

3) Proof and remediation: procurement wants defined remediation credits if p95 breach persists for >30 minutes after mitigation steps are initiated.

I've attached a short RFC with our expectations (finx_slo_rfc.pdf). Can we get a proposed amendment draft this week so legal can begin review?

Best,
Sam
Sam Ellis
Head of Infrastructure
FinX

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Latency SLO: temporal boundaries & fallback commitments

Hi Sam — appreciate the clear asks and the RFC. I looped in Laura (contracts) and Karthik (platform) to align on feasibility. High-level proposal below; attaching a draft amendment so your legal can start a parallel pass (proposed_amendment_draft.docx).

Quick summary of our recommended approach (draft):
- Operational SLOs (hosted API): p50 = 120ms, p95 = 600ms measured at the request ingress point for the customer tenant.
- Measurement cadence: sample end-to-end latency every second; compute rolling percentiles over a 5-minute window for operational alerting and a 30-minute rolling window for short-term remediation triggers. For contractual measurement (billing/credits) we use a 24-hour rolling aggregation with epoched 1-hour buckets to avoid short-lived noise.
- Burst carveout: automatic transient carveout up to 10 minutes per region per 24-hour period, subject to evidence of a traffic spike (>=3x baseline QPS sustained for >60s). Additional carveouts can be negotiated as part of seasonal plans.
- Fallback/rollback: automated routing to a compatible, lower-latency model variant (quantized or smaller model) with an SLA of p95 <= 450ms post-fallback. Fallback action will be visible via the Console webhook and a /events callback to your ops channel.
- Remediation credits: if a p95 breach persists beyond 30 minutes after mitigation (canary/rollback) is started, we propose a credit ladder (0-1hr = 5% monthly usage credit, 1-3hr = 12.5%, >3hr escalates to account review).

Why this is conservative vs your 5-minute-only ask: very short contractual measurement windows can be sensitive to sampling jitter, single-node GC events, and transient routing anomalies. We therefore separate operational alerting (5-minute) from contractual accounting (24-hour epoched aggregation) to balance responsiveness with fairness.

Next steps:
- Laura: can legal start redline pass on the attached amendment?
- Karthik/Marcus: can you confirm we can guarantee fallback model routing and the 10-minute carveout logic from an infra standpoint?

Sam — if that aligns, we'll push the redline to DocuSign and provide a short runbook and evidence playbook for your ops team.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed amendment & rollback playbook (finx)

Sam / Oliver — attaching the draft amendment and a short rollback playbook excerpt inline below. I also pasted the DocuSign link at the bottom for a redline/countersign path: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEFG12345

Excerpt — Rollback & fallback playbook (summary):
1) Detection: Alert fired when 5-minute rolling p95 exceeds 600ms and 30-minute rolling p95 > 550ms.
2) Triage (0-5 minutes): Ops runbook checks the Console trace for GC/node failures, and our system triggers automatic canary to 5% of traffic routed to fallback model. Webhook /webhooks/slo-events posts status.
3) Canary (5-15 minutes): If canary p95 < 450ms and user acceptance checks pass, escalate to 30% routing to fallback.
4) Full fallback (15-30 minutes): If canary successful, auto-commit fallback for up to 10 minutes carveout period. Manual escalation required for >10 minutes and additional contract carveout.
5) Evidence: Console trace logs, sampling histograms, and ingress RTT snapshots included in the evidence bundle for credits.

Please review — if FinX legal is comfortable we'll route the draft to DocuSign for countersign. If you want to tweak the carveout duration (10 -> 20 minutes) we can discuss as a seasonal amendment.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
